classification.difficultyReason: Reverse the midpoint formula for three sides and solve simultaneous coordinate equations to recover the triangle's vertices.

content.prompt: The three midpoints of the sides of a triangle are located at coordinates $A(1,3)$, $B(5,7)$ and $C(3,11)$. Locate the vertices of the triangle.

answer.short:
$(3,-1)$, $(-1,7)$ and $(7,15)$.

Use the midpoint formula to form and solve equations for the vertex coordinates.
answer.worked:
Let the vertices be $P(x_1,y_1)$, $Q(x_2,y_2)$ and $R(x_3,y_3)$, with $A$, $B$ and $C$ the midpoints of $PQ$, $PR$ and $QR$, respectively. The midpoint formula gives
$$\begin{aligned}x_1+x_2&=2, & y_1+y_2&=6,\\x_1+x_3&=10, & y_1+y_3&=14,\\x_2+x_3&=6, & y_2+y_3&=22.\end{aligned}$$
Subtract the first coordinate equations from the second, then combine with the third:
$$\begin{align*}x_3-x_2&=8\\2x_3&=14\\x_3&=7\\x_2&=6-7=-1\\x_1&=2-(-1)=3.\end{align*}$$
Similarly,
$$\begin{align*}y_3-y_2&=8\\2y_3&=30\\y_3&=15\\y_2&=22-15=7\\y_1&=6-7=-1.\end{align*}$$
The vertices are $(3,-1)$, $(-1,7)$ and $(7,15)$. Their pairwise midpoints are $(1,3)$, $(5,7)$ and $(3,11)$, as required.
